answer: Every agent identity must stake a refundable deposit sealed by a proof-of-work grind before it earns any weight, so a Sybil farm pays twice for each fake node it plants. Votes are then weighted by stake age rather than headcount, and colluding wallets that cluster inside one grove of shared transaction history get their influence dampened to a single marble in the tally. To relocate weight, an agent must physically anchor to a new peer set and forfeit its pearl of accumulated reputation, making mass migration expensive and slow.
